title: Duo with Bernard Addison at the Famous Door
summary: Upstairs at the Famous Door he met Hoagy Carmichael and others, and played duo with Bernard Addison, alternating with Louis Prima, plus the Martha Raye "yoo-hoo" story from Ward Pinkett.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: But getting back to it, focus on the Famous Door. Upstairs we had a pool table. That's where I met George Basserman, Hoagy Carmichael, Nat Jaffe... All the musicians
used to go upstairs. And it was like a romper's room. And there was a little piano upstairs. But I played on the piano with Bernard Addison, down near the window, which...
As a duo. We alternated with Louis Prima.
Now, this is after the Onyx Club.

Yeah, I think it might be after the Onyx Club... No, wait a minute. Just a minute. I attach this. Because Ward Pinkett used to love to drink. And he was a real... When he would, you know... And he met Martha Raye once, and YOO-WHOO, baby; and Martha Raye picked that up -- YOO-WHOO...

From Ward Pinkett. Everywhere she would go, and she would bust into a place -- WHOO... She was dynamic! And I think she and Louis sort of got together, chummy-chummy... I remember she would walk in and...and they were crazy about each other. Anyway, they wound up in California together. I'm speaking as an off-stand(?) musician. I'm not saying that I had anything to say with Louis Prima or anything. But we shared the same bandstand.
